title: Closed Form for the Rotation Fixed-Point Count: |Fix(r_i)| = 2^gcd(n, i)
description: Answers the rotation half of the second open question of burnside-counting-oq-04-oq-01-oq-01, which asked to replace the per-n kernel decide of the Burnside fixed-point sum by a closed form Σ_{g ∈ D_n} |Fix(g)| = Σ_r 2^gcd(n,r) + (reflection contribution). Where the parent evaluates each fixed-point sum one length at a time with kernel decide, this entry proves the generic rotation term with no computation and uniformly in n: the binary colourings of the n-cycle fixed by the rotation x ↦ x + i number exactly 2^gcd(n, i.val), two to the number of orbits of the rotation. The proof identifies fixed colourings with functions constant on the cosets of the cyclic subgroup ⟨i⟩ ≤ ZMod n: invariant_zsmul upgrades invariance under +i to invariance under +k·i for every integer k by two-sided Int.induction_on, giving the bijection rotFixedEquiv : {c // IsRotInvariant i c} ≃ (ZMod n ⧸ zmultiples i → Fin 2); card_quotient_zmultiples evaluates |ZMod n ⧸ ⟨i⟩| = gcd(n, i.val) via Lagrange (index_mul_card), Nat.card_zmultiples and ZMod.addOrderOf_coe (addOrderOf i = n / gcd(n, i.val)); and card_rotFixed reads off 2^gcd(n, i.val). Corollaries recover the two extreme cases (i = 0 fixes all 2^n colourings; a step coprime to n fixes only the 2 constant colourings) and the rotation sub-sums of the parent's totals (Σ_{i : ZMod 5} = 40, Σ_{i : ZMod 6} = 84) directly from the formula. Only kernel decide on closed ℕ arithmetic is used for the finite cross-checks; #print axioms reports only propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound (no native_decide, no sorryAx).

meta.author: Burnside / Pólya theory; formalized for lean-genius (researcher-10)

mathlibDependencies.description: Nat.card (zmultiples i) = addOrderOf i. Together with ZMod.addOrderOf_coe gives |⟨i⟩| = n / gcd(n, i.val).
addOrderOf (i : ZMod n) = n / gcd(n, i.val) for n ≠ 0; supplies the order of the cyclic subgroup ⟨i⟩.
Lagrange's theorem in additive form: (zmultiples i).index · Nat.card (zmultiples i) = Nat.card (ZMod n); solved for the coset count = gcd(n, i.val).
Characterise the coset relation a ~ b ⇔ b - a ∈ ⟨i⟩, used to push an invariant colouring through the quotient and to pull a quotient function back to an invariant colouring in rotFixedEquiv.
|α → β| = |β|^|α|; converts the colourings-on-the-quotient count to 2^|ZMod n ⧸ ⟨i⟩|.

originalContributions: card_rotFixed: a closed form Fintype.card {c : ZMod n → Fin 2 // ∀ p, c (p + i) = c p} = 2^gcd(n, i.val), uniform in n with no per-length computation — Mathlib has no rotation fixed-point count for cyclic colourings

invariant_zsmul: invariance of a colouring under the single shift +i extends to invariance under +k·i for every integer k, by two-sided Int.induction_on with an explicit subtract-i form — the statement that an invariant colouring is constant on each coset of ⟨i⟩
rotFixedEquiv: the bijection {c // IsRotInvariant i c} ≃ (ZMod n ⧸ zmultiples i → Fin 2), realising fixed colourings as functions on the coset space via Quotient.liftOn' and a pullback
card_quotient_zmultiples: |ZMod n ⧸ ⟨i⟩| = gcd(n, i.val) (the orbit count of the rotation x ↦ x + i) from Lagrange, Nat.card_zmultiples and ZMod.addOrderOf_coe

card_rotFixed_zero / card_rotFixed_of_gcd_eq_one: the extreme cases i = 0 (all 2^n colourings) and gcd(n, i.val) = 1 (only the 2 constant colourings); rotation_sum_five / rotation_sum_six: the rotation sub-sums 40 and 84 of the parent's Burnside totals 80 and 156, read off the formula by kernel decide
meta.assumptions: None. Fully verified, 0 axioms, 0 sorries, and no native_decide: the headline closed form card_rotFixed and all corollaries depend only on the foundational axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound (confirmed via #print axioms — in particular no Lean.ofReduceBool and no sorryAx). The finite cross-checks rotation_sum_five / rotation_sum_six use ordinary kernel decide on closed ℕ arithmetic.

overview.historicalContext: Burnside's lemma counts orbits of a finite group action as the average number of fixed points. For the rotation group ℤ/nℤ acting on the beads of an n-cycle, the fixed-point count of the rotation by i is a classical ingredient of the necklace and bracelet formulas: a colouring is fixed iff it is constant on the orbits of the rotation, and the rotation x ↦ x + i has exactly gcd(n, i) orbits, so it fixes 2^gcd(n, i) binary colourings. Summing 2^gcd(n,i) over i and averaging is Pólya's necklace count; adjoining the reflections gives the bracelet count A000029. The grandparent burnside-counting-oq-04-oq-01-oq-01 evaluated the full dihedral fixed-point sum length by length with kernel decide and asked, as its second open question, for a closed form replacing that computation. This entry settles the rotation contribution of that closed form, uniformly in n.
overview.problemStatement: Prove, with no per-n computation and uniformly in n, that the binary colourings of the n-cycle fixed by the rotation x ↦ x + i number exactly 2^gcd(n, i.val) — the rotation half of the closed form Σ_{g ∈ D_n} |Fix(g)| = Σ_r 2^gcd(n,r) + (reflection contribution) requested by the parent's second open question.
overview.text: A colouring c : ZMod n → Fin 2 is fixed by the rotation x ↦ x + i exactly when c (p + i) = c p for all p, equivalently when c is constant on each coset of the cyclic subgroup ⟨i⟩ ≤ ZMod n. The coset space ZMod n ⧸ ⟨i⟩ has gcd(n, i.val) points (the orbit count), so the fixed colourings are in bijection with functions on a gcd(n, i.val)-point set, of which there are 2^gcd(n, i.val).
overview.proofStrategy: IsRotInvariant i c says c (p + i) = c p for all p. invariant_zsmul upgrades this to c (p + k·i) = c p for every integer k by Int.induction_on (using the subtract-i form c (p - i) = c p for the negative branch), so an invariant colouring is constant on each coset of zmultiples i. rotFixedEquiv builds the bijection RotFixed n i ≃ (ZMod n ⧸ zmultiples i → Fin 2): forward by Quotient.liftOn' (well-defined because b ~ a ⇒ b = a + k·i ⇒ c b = c a), backward by pullback along QuotientAddGroup.mk (invariant because (p+i) - p = i ∈ ⟨i⟩). card_quotient_zmultiples computes |ZMod n ⧸ ⟨i⟩| = gcd(n, i.val): Nat.card_zmultiples and ZMod.addOrderOf_coe give |⟨i⟩| = n / gcd(n, i.val), and Lagrange's index_mul_card with |ZMod n| = n solves index = gcd(n, i.val). Finally card_rotFixed chains Fintype.card_congr, Fintype.card_fun and Fintype.card_fin to read off 2^gcd(n, i.val).
keyInsights: Fixed colourings of a rotation are exactly the functions constant on its orbits, and the orbits of x ↦ x + i are the cosets of the cyclic subgroup ⟨i⟩ — so the count is 2 raised to the number of cosets, with no enumeration over colourings

The number of orbits is |ZMod n ⧸ ⟨i⟩| = gcd(n, i.val), obtained purely structurally from Lagrange and the order of i (addOrderOf i = n / gcd(n, i.val)) — the gcd appears as the index of a cyclic subgroup, not by a counting argument

Extending single-shift invariance to k·i invariance for all integers k is the technical core (invariant_zsmul); a two-sided integer induction with an explicit subtract-i lemma covers the negative multiples that a one-sided Nat induction misses

The closed form is honest about scope: it settles the rotation summand Σ_r 2^gcd(n,r); the reflection contribution (parity-dependent in n and i) is left to future work, and the parent still settles the full bracelet counts computationally
prerequisites: Group actions, orbits, and fixed points; the orbit-counting (Burnside) lemma as background
Quotient groups, cosets, Lagrange's theorem (index · order = group order), and the order of an element
ZMod n, cyclic subgroups zmultiples, gcd and addOrderOf in Mathlib

This file proves the generic rotation term 2^gcd(n, i.val) uniformly in n (no computation), plus the namespace, the Coloring/IsRotInvariant/RotFixed definitions and their Fintype instances. Honest scope: only the rotation half; the reflection contribution is left to future work; everything is axiom-free (kernel decide, no native_decide).

crossReferences.description: Answers the rotation half of the second open question of oq-04-oq-01-oq-01: replaces the per-n kernel decide of the fixed-point sum by the closed form |Fix(r_i)| = 2^gcd(n, i.val), uniform in n, and recovers the parent's rotation sub-sums 40 (n=5) and 84 (n=6) directly from it.
Extends the concrete dihedral fixed-point computation toward a symbolic per-element formula by giving the rotation elements a closed fixed-point count 2^gcd(n, i.val) valid for all n.

conclusion.summary: The binary colourings of the n-cycle fixed by the rotation x ↦ x + i number exactly 2^gcd(n, i.val), proved uniformly in n with no per-length computation: fixed colourings are functions on the coset space ZMod n ⧸ ⟨i⟩, which has gcd(n, i.val) points by Lagrange and the order of i. This settles the rotation summand Σ_r 2^gcd(n,r) of the closed form requested by the parent's second open question, with 0 axioms beyond propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound.
conclusion.implications: Each rotation fixed-point count is now closed-form rather than kernel-decided, so the rotation part of the Burnside / Pólya necklace and bracelet sums needs no enumeration at any length; combined with a reflection fixed-point formula it would give a fully closed form for A000029(n) with no computation. The same coset-space bijection generalises verbatim to k colours (Fin k → 2 ↦ k, giving k^gcd(n,i)).
openQuestions: Prove the reflection fixed-point counts in closed form: for n odd each of the n axes fixes 2^((n+1)/2) colourings, and for n even the n/2 vertex-axes fix 2^(n/2+1) and the n/2 edge-axes fix 2^(n/2), completing Σ_{g ∈ D_n} |Fix(g)| = Σ_r 2^gcd(n,r) + (reflection contribution).
Combine the rotation closed form with the reflection closed form and average to derive the bracelet count b(n) = A000029(n) symbolically, eliminating the parent's per-n kernel decide entirely.
